text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday, prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The central Bank announced the introduction of a new five-lat banknote with enhanced security features from March 27.

- The leader of the Latvian Social Democrats, Juris Bojars, sued Prime Minister Andris Shkele for defamation, referring to Shkele's remarks on TV that the leaders of the party are KGB officers and graduates of Soviet military schools although Bojars is indeed a former KGB officer and a Soviet military school graduate.

- The general prosecutor's office is to protest against the refusal of the court of Daugavpils to consider the case of Alexei Vidavskii, the mayor of the city, who might be banned from taking office for being an active member of the Communist party after January 13, 1991.

- The European Integration Bureau's terminology and translation centre was opened in Riga with the main aim to translate EU laws and regulations into Latvian and Latvian legislative acts into English and French. The centre hopes to have the bulk of EU documents translated in five years.
- Foreign Ministry Secretary of State, Maris Riekstins, visit to Belarus was postponed due to failure to agree on the agenda of talks in the proper time.
- The WEU Secretary General, Jose Cutillero, is on a two-day official visit in Latvia.
- Andris Argalis of Fatherland and Freedom and Juris Ritins of the Democratic Party Saimnieks were elected vice-mayors of Riga.
- The number of standing committees in Riga municipality was reduced from 11 to 9.
- The basic principles for privatisation of Ventspils Nafta and Lasam, pipeline operator are to be considered on April 1.
- President Guntis Ulmanis left for on one-day visit to Helsinki to discuss the results of the U.S.-Russian summit with President Martti Ahtisaari.
- The number of computers sold in Latvia is doubling every six months.

- The head of the transport ministry's transit division, Zigmars Priede, believes that the work of Latvian customs is the main hindrance to transit development in Latvia. In April the ministry will submit draft amendmendments to customs cargo transit legislation.
